what_this_is: Honest field-accuracy evaluation of candidate plant-disease models, measured on 215 real in-field photographs from the PlantDoc TEST split (NOT PlantVillage lab photos). Phase 2 exit criteria, docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md 1.1.

test_set.why: PlantVillage is 54k lab photos on plain backgrounds. Models trained on it report ~99% accuracy but collapse on real farmer photos (soil, other leaves, shadow, blur). PlantDoc is real in-field imagery, so it measures what actually matters.
test_set.sampling: up to 10 images per class, taken from the official test split

results_top1_top3_on_field_photos.note: model card advertises 99.83% accuracy -- on its own lab-photo eval split

headline: The lab-vs-field gap is the entire story: every PlantVillage-trained model lands between 3.7% and 40% top-1 on real field photos despite advertising 95-99%+ on lab test splits. Training domain mattered far more than architecture or model-card claims.

selected_model_threshold_sweep.note: Confidence gate calibration for the selected model. 'precision' = accuracy on the images the cascade actually answers; the rest are honestly declined.

previous_model_at_its_old_gate.why_this_was_dangerous: It answered confidently on half of all real photos and was wrong roughly 3 times out of 4 when it did.

data_leakage_check.concern: The selected model was trained on PlantDoc and its model card is empty, so its train/test split cannot be verified from the Hub. If it had trained on this test split, the 73% would be inflated.
evidence_against_leakage: Mean top-1 probability is only 0.534 overall and 0.598 even when correct; memorized training images typically produce near-1.0 confidence.
Only 1.9% of test images exceed p>0.95.
73% top-1 sits in the normal published range for PlantDoc benchmarks (~70%), not at the suspicious 95-100% a leaked split would produce.
data_leakage_check.residual_risk: Cannot be fully eliminated without retraining from a known-clean split. If the report needs an airtight number, fine-tune on the PlantDoc TRAIN split and re-measure on TEST.

honest_limitations: 215 images, 27 classes -- small enough that per-class figures are noisy; treat the headline top-1/top-3 as the reliable numbers.
PlantDoc itself is web-scraped, so some label noise exists.
The model covers 28 classes across 13 crops. Rice, wheat, cotton and sugarcane -- major Indian crops -- are NOT covered by any of these public checkpoints.
Field accuracy of 73% top-1 means roughly 1 in 4 raw predictions is wrong, which is exactly why the confidence gate and honest-decline stage exist.
